speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Fourth time lucky for me on this Motion.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: This year, we commemorated 50 years of National Service (NS).

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: And much like the turbulent circumstances of our Independence, National Service was something that we had to embark upon out of necessity.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: At the time of separation, Singapore was faced with a host of threats, including the Konfrontasi with Indonesia, insurgency from the Malayan Communist Party and communal violence.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The British forces remained to provide security but, in 1967, barely three years after Independence, the British forces also announced their withdrawal.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: At this time, Singapore had very little in way of financial resources and a booming population following the post-war Baby Boom.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: It has been 50 years since the Enlistment Act was passed and there have been many changes in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Our security threats and our approach to NS have evolved with us.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The focus of this committee was to ensure that support for NS remains strong in the population and that NSmen, employers and family members all have a shared sense of duty for their part in this process.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The focus of this committee was to improve the lives of NSmen and to make compliance with NS obligations easier for all stakeholders, without compromising training needs – a difficult balance, indeed, that has required thoughtful, well-calibrated policies.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The NS50 events from July to September were particularly moving, with the theme "From my generation to yours", bringing together earlier and current generations of NSmen.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Prime Minister Lee himself made a moving speech at the final event last week, sharing his own experiences in the army and ending with the importance of passing the NS torch from his generation to the subsequent ones.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: NS is an important rite of passage for us, and I am heartened that many understand and appreciate its importance.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: My main interest in this Motion is to understand how NS will fit into the future roles the military will be required to perform and the constraints we face.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Traditionally, NS has largely involved starting in the military and with the majority of the cohort going through a Basic Military Training (BMT) that is modelled on infantry training.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: This shared experience is an important part of the bonding that NSmen feel intuitively when they meet one another.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: We all have the same experience going through BMT, dealing with NS sergeants and the same thing that we laugh about when we watch "Ah Boys to Men".

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: First, military technology improves at a tremendous pace.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: New inventions can render previous methods of warfare otiose.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: One vivid example is the use of drones in warfare.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: A BBC story on a United States (US) drone pilot was eye opening.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The drone pilot, for example, could have breakfast at home, send his daughter to school, then go to a drone control centre a short drive from home and pilot a drone based thousands of miles away in the Middle East.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: It will be office hours for him but night time in the country of operations.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The precision of such technology allows the pilot to see the targets clearly at night, attack with precision and take photographs after the damage has been inflicted.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: After a day of fighting, which could still be office hours for the drone pilot, he could go back home at night and have dinner with his family.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Yet, even drone-fighter pilots go through a very high incidence of post-traumatic stress disorder.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: So, they, too, seem to face the psychological stresses that other combatants face.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Aerial drone warfare is just one component of increasingly automated forms of warfare, although it is probably the one that captures the imagination most readily.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: At the recent NS PRIDE Day awards, I was quite happy to see that even our own NSmen have found numerous uses of drone technology and I assume that because this is NS PRIDE Day awards, it is in the public domain.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: For example, drones are used in naval operations.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: They are used for surveillance and intelligence gathering.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: In the army, they can also be used for reconnaissance operations and security patrolling.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: All of these things used to be done by infantrymen who had to face the danger of enemy fire.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: However, would this rapid use of technology make it, first of all, difficult for NSmen to catch up?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Will our NSmen be able to keep up with this increasingly advanced form of warfare?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: And how will dealing with automated warfare be built into the drills that our NSmen go through, perhaps either in lieu of or maybe in addition to the old field crafts we learnt?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The second type of threats we have to prepare for is on the other end of the technology spectrum.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The difference between terror and conventional warfare is that conventional warfare, of course, if you comply with the rules of war, is a military-and-military exercise.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Civilian populations are not, at least in theory, meant to be targeted.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: On the other hand, terrorists have complete disregard for this principle.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Yet, as these threats become a much larger face of the type of threats we face, would we see a larger role for NSmen in dealing with this new type of threat?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The final aspect that I have to deal with is how we deal with the limitations and constraints.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: This is a constant theme that the Ministry has dealt with over the years.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: In the early days of NS, we had a population boom with high unemployment.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: So, pulling people into NS did not have as big an economic impact.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: So, the Ministry of Defence (MINDEF) will have to be able to make do with a much smaller population.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: At the same time, MINDEF's available training spaces are also getting reduced due to competing needs for land in land-scarce Singapore.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: I have been quite impressed by MINDEF's efforts at working around these constraints.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: As an infantryman, I did my basic training.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: I learnt, well, the old M16 rifle, and I barely passed my shooting test.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: I have shared in this House how the SAR-21 doubled my productivity.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: I managed to get a Marksman the first time I tried.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The range I used was also a multi-storey rifle range.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: So, that meant it could have many more times the number of people doing the training.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: So, this seems to be MINDEF's way of adapting.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: It used better technology to get the same outcomes by using less land and less resources.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: While these are admirable adaptions which, basically, are the classic productivity improvements where you are getting more out of less, will we be able to achieve better outcomes by changing the game altogether?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: For example, if we are looking at the face of warfare where you do not need very large amounts of manpower to fight wars or to man aircraft, do we need different forms of training altogether which would significantly change the type of training areas we need and the type of people we need to have trained?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: In this Motion, I was hoping to raise raw themes to give the Ministry a platform to, basically, share the vision of NS perhaps for the next 50 years, even as we move forward to the first 50 with strong support from our population.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: As the Member has not used his full 20 minutes, I will allow one more speaker.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I am speaking in my capacity as a Member of the Government Parliamentary Committee (GPC) for Defence and from the perspective of a mother, daughter, wife and maybe future mother-in-law.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This is a special year as we mark 50 years of NS.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Tributes have come from many sectors and I think it is important for us here in Parliament to dedicate a few moments to pay a special tribute to all our NSmen, past and present, for their sacrifices to protect our only home.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Changi Airport has joined in the NS50 tributes, too, with a 5.5-metre NS statue at Terminal 3.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This life-sized infantry soldier stands proudly against the Singapore flag and had been inspired by the NS Landmark at the BMT Centre in Pulau Tekong.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We live in challenging times and have to be constantly on our guard to defend Singapore against potential external threats and terrorists.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Pick up any newspaper now on any given day and you will see the escalating terrorist threats faced by cities all over the world.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: More than ever, we need our NSmen to be well-trained and on the alert to ensure our security and survival.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: NS has evolved tremendously over the last few decades and has become the pride of Singapore.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: NS is also an important rite of passage and integral part of Singapore life.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is heartening for me to hear from so many parents their support for NS and how proud they are of their family members who have learnt and benefited from the discipline and rigour of NS training.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They marvel at how their sons mature and become so fit during NS.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Their increased confidence, mental and physical toughness bode very well for our future.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Going forward, NS will evolve even further due to technological advances.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Information technology (IT) and artificial intelligence (AI) will change how NS will be managed.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We must prepare to keep up with these advancements.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is important to ensure the highest level of safety even as they undergo realistic training.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, insurance is necessary so that in the event of incidents, families need not go to Court to claim, which will help to reduce hardship and additional emotional trauma.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Every injury and life lost is one less fighting force for Singapore.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: With such a small fighting force due to our small population and low fertility rates, we cannot afford to be careless or suffer from any oversight.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Utmost care must be exercised at every level even as we strive for realistic training.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Our men and their families must have peace of mind so that they can put their best into their training.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: There should be multiple channels for feedback from our NSmen to report on blind spots, negligence and abuses, as well as ideas and suggestions for improvement and greater efficiency.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In fact, recently, I have received feedback from our younger generation about including women in NS, albeit in different roles.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: A few girls even expressed that women could contribute more significantly to NS, whether in similar combat roles, logistics, resource management, administrative support, IT, medical, amongst others.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I am heartened by the enthusiasm of our young women and impressed by their awareness of the various scopes of different roles necessary for the defence of our country.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Let us continue to explore how women can contribute even more to increase their roles in Singapore’s defence.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This also ties in with our national effort to boost the health and fitness of all Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: As a community, we should support our NSmen in this endeavour, and let us all keep fit together, young and old, children and the elderly.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: An active, healthy and fit community is also an important component of national defence.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Let us reaffirm our commitment to our national defence and pledge our full support for our NSmen to work together for Singapore's defence and security.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We may be a small nation but we are a force to be reckoned with.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We will not back down from intimidation or threats and we can give as good as it gets.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Our will and determination to protect our home will be the most powerful shield against any threat.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Every single one of us – men, women and children – will stand our ground and fight to the last to defend Singapore, our home.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Would the Senior Minister of State like to respond?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Since Independence, this Government has been consistent and unwavering in its commitment towards strong defence and security that can only be possible with NS, due to our limited manpower.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: National conscription is a difficult policy for any country to introduce and just as challenging to maintain.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Fifty years ago, with our nation’s very survival at stake, with Independence thrust upon her precipitously and without any military to protect her sovereignty, the government of the day took that onerous but courageous step to introduce NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Then, Singapore was poor and undeveloped, and there was no certainty that we could even succeed as a nation or build a credible military to protect our borders and interests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: After 50 years, and a million NSmen who have performed this sacred duty honourably and faithfully, including many NSmen Members of Parliament here, we can take pride that together, we have built up a strong SAF and Home Team, respected and able to protect Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Why did our founding leaders begin NS then, even though it was politically challenging and unpopular in a Singapore that was impoverished and beset with so many other economic and social problems?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As our founding Prime Minister Mr Lee Kuan Yew revealed in 2012, and I quote, "From the day we started, I knew that we needed a strong SAF, and I believe that remains today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Without a strong SAF, there is no economic future, there is no security." This truism remains.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Today, the external threats may have changed in nature, but are no less threatening, either to the safety of our citizens or the sovereignty of our nation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Yes, today, this House sits in a very different Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Certainly, we are more prosperous and stable with the SAF and the Home Team keeping Singapore safe daily.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The Police and the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) work hard to maintain law and order, responding to all types of emergencies, and are prepared to deal with any threat.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our crime rates are low and, while the terrorist threat is a grave one, our security forces are vigilant and prepared to deal with an attack when it comes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: NS receives very strong support from all Members of this House, from employers and citizens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In our polls, more than 90% of citizens support NS and our national defence policies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I am deeply gratified, but MINDEF and SAF will never take that support for granted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Neither will it lull us into a complacency to let down our guard to protect this nation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Indeed, that strong support from this House and the public spurs us to further strengthen SAF, to modernise its processes, ensure greater accountability of the resources given to it and engage its soldiers better.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our NSmen form the bedrock of our defence and security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will continue to improve NS, help our NSmen perform their duties more effectively and recognise their contributions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Today, pre-enlistees from the Home Team and SAF can indicate their vocational interest for NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have also reduced the waiting time for enlistment and introduced life and personal accident insurance coverage for all NSmen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We agree with Ms Joan Pereira that we must do everything possible to prevent loss of life or bodily harm to our soldiers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We owe this to the young men who give of their best serving the nation, and to their parents who entrust their sons to us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: SAF will continue to regularly review and strengthen its safety systems, with regular inspections and external professional advice.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We fully agree with Mr Vikram Nair and Ms Joan Pereira, too, that the Next Generation NSmen must adapt their roles and responsibilities to a changing security environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Today, NSmen are already trained to operate our new air defence weapons, unmanned aerial vehicles and use data analytic tools for maritime threats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We agree with Mr Vikram Nair that NS roles will be further optimised through the use of technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Going forward, more NSmen will operate unmanned platforms, use AI, data analytics and robotics to act as force multipliers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, SAF is developing an Unmanned Ground Vehicle armed with a suite of sensors which enable our forces to respond to security threats quickly and effectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Even as we expand and strengthen NSmen’s capabilities to defend our home against changing threats, societal support remains the strongest form of motivation to our NSmen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This year, we are heartened that different sectors of the community have come forward to commemorate NS50 together, including Members of Parliament here who hosted appreciation ceremonies in their constituencies for father and son NSmen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Hundreds more employers reaffirmed their commitment to the defence of Singapore at combined rededication ceremonies in July this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: More than 500 businesses and organisations have introduced initiatives to commemorate NS50, including offering discounts and privileges for NSmen to enjoy with their families.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But most encouraging is the groundswell of spontaneous individual stories on social media from tens of thousands of NSmen and members of the community.
